title: Growing-volume log-domain Lyapunov core-tail stress
question: Does the R-417 log-domain Lyapunov/core-tail corridor persist under a bounded growing-volume Q3 stress, without treating a finite envelope as a uniform theorem?

new_perspective.principle: Stress the same source-independent finite Q3 construction in volume as well as cutoff, while retaining the tail drift, induced-core gap, tail mass and boundary rate as separate quantities.
route: Keep the R-417 Hamiltonian, coordinate basis, log-Gibbs reconstruction, momentum conductance and alpha/theta grid unchanged.
Add volumes three and four at low cutoffs so the conditional-prefix geometry grows rather than only the one-site oscillator cutoff.
Evaluate every right/left prefix row and retain minimum/maximum aggregates, including rows with no nonempty tail.
Reconstruct the same grid independently and use hostile sign, normalization, volume-omission and disconnected-core mutations.
If a drift or core envelope collapses, preserve the finite diagnostic and register a route-local obstruction; if it persists, use it only to sharpen the analytic target.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A surviving finite growing-volume envelope identifies a better stress target for a common-core estimate. It does not establish volume uniformity, phase selection, OS/KMS/GNS coercivity, a continuum limit or a physical gap.

finite_theorem.log_domain: For each finite Q3 Hamiltonian, log-sum-exp reconstructs a normalized positive coordinate law without direct-density underflow.
finite_theorem.lyapunov: For positive conditional weights and symmetric momentum conductances, V_i=exp(alpha*(log(pi_max)-log(pi_i))) and -LV/V are evaluated on each declared tail.
finite_theorem.core: The induced core graph is renormalized by its core mass and its projected positive eigenvalue is recorded separately from the full graph gap.
finite_theorem.stress: The finite test covers a prescribed volume/cutoff/beta/orientation grid. It neither quantifies a supremum over missing volumes nor proves that any observed minimum is volume-independent.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar positivity, the conservative core-tail envelope and finite grid bookkeeping; it does not formalize the Q3 matrix diagonalization, conditional distributions, spectral calculations or any volume/continuum limit.

promotion_criteria: Replace this bounded stress by an analytic volume-, cutoff-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform drift estimate on one Hamiltonian common core.
Prove a matching induced-core Schur/Poincare and boundary-capacity estimate, not just a finite eigenvalue minimum.
Control the actual R-399 likelihood observables in the same two-sided form norm before transferring through R-415 or revisiting GNS coercivity.
stop_conditions: A validated nonpositive tail drift, disconnected induced core or uncontrolled tail mass is a route-local obstruction, not a physical conclusion.
Independent disagreement stops promotion and requires repair of model construction, log normalization, conductance or core scaling.
Finite persistence remains diagnostic only and cannot close C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, a QFT mass gap or a continuum theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite growing-volume log-domain Lyapunov/core-tail stress. No volume-, cutoff-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform drift or gap, no common Hamiltonian core, no global Poincare theorem, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no physical mass gap, no continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: A bounded growing-volume stress can expose a finite collapse or strengthen the list of analytic inputs; it cannot turn finite positive envelopes into uniform coercivity or a physical theorem.
